transcript:
User: Yeah, I got a voicemail from you people. This better be quick, I've got three jobs waiting.
Agent: Got it, I hear you — I’ll keep this tight.  

When you’re out on those jobs and a new customer calls in, who usually picks up the phone for you?
User: Usually my wife, but why do you need to know that?
Agent: Makes sense, thanks for telling me.  

The only reason I ask is we help businesses like yours stop losing jobs when a call comes in and no one can grab it right away — are you running into missed calls now, or is your wife able to catch most of them?
User: Everyone says they can help. She's handling it fine. Why should I believe you're any different?
Agent: Totally fair, I get that — you’re busy and you’ve heard a lot of promises.  

So if your wife misses, say, even one or two calls on a busy day, what does that usually turn into for you — is that like a $500–$1,000 job gone, or more?
User: That's none of your business. Why do you need to know how much I make? Sounds fishy to me.
Agent: Yeah, that’s fair — I don’t need to know your numbers, and I’m not asking how much you make.  

All we actually do is make sure when your wife can’t grab the phone, the call still gets answered and booked for you — do you ever have times where it just rings out or goes to voicemail?
User: Sure, it happens. But why would I trust you with my business calls? Sounds like a scam.
Agent: Totally get why you’d say that — you don’t want some random company messing with your customers.  

So when a call does slip through the cracks right now, do you usually just let it go, or are you calling people back later when you get a minute?
User: We call back when we can. But why do you care? This feels like a waste of time.
Agent: Totally hear you — if it doesn’t help you, it *is* a waste of time.  

Since you’re already just calling people back when you can, what actually happens with the ones you *don’t* get around to — do they usually call you back, or do you figure they probably go to someone else?
User: They might go elsewhere, but I can't chase every call. I’ve got plumbing to do, not phone tag.
Agent: Yeah, that makes total sense — you’re supposed to be under sinks, not glued to a phone.  

Roughly how many calls a day would you say hit voicemail or don’t get answered the first time?
User: I don't track every call. I'm too busy working. Why does that matter to you?
Agent: Totally fine, I wouldn’t expect you to track it — you’re on the tools, not in a call center.  

Given that some of those callers “might go elsewhere,” would it be useful if those missed calls automatically turned into booked jobs or at least solid voicemails *without* you or your wife chasing them?
User: Sounds too good to be true. Everyone promises miracles. What's the catch?
Agent: Yeah, I don’t blame you — “miracle” stuff usually is a scam.  

The real “catch” is simple: we only help with the calls you’d otherwise miss, turning those into booked jobs or clear messages, and you pay only if you decide it’s worth the extra work it brings — would you want me to walk you through, in plain English, how that would plug into your wife answering the phone now?
User: I don't have time for this, and I’m not convinced. Thanks, but no thanks. Bye.
Agent: Totally understand, I know you’re slammed and I appreciate you giving me a minute. If you ever get to the point where the missed calls really start bugging you, you’re welcome to get back in touch and we can walk through it quickly. Have a good one and stay safe on those jobs.
